title: Home Battery Incentives in New York City (2026): NYSERDA Storage Program
desc: NYC home battery incentives for 2026: NYSERDA's Residential Energy Storage Program pays per kWh for batteries up to 25 kWh, more in Disadvantaged Communities. The federal credit has ended.
h1: Home Battery Incentives in New York City
badge: Paid per kWh, up to 25 kWh
lead: Unlike on Long Island, a New York City home does not need solar panels to get a state battery incentive. NYSERDA's Residential Energy Storage Program helps pay for home batteries of 25 kWh or less, with more for income-eligible homes and Disadvantaged Communities. Here is how it works and who it suits.
cards_heading: What battery incentives exist in New York City
cards_intro: We re-read NYSERDA's home energy storage pages on October 3, 2026. NYSERDA posts its current per-kWh rate on a regional dashboard rather than on the program page, so we do not quote a dollar figure here. Ask any contractor to show it on your quote.

cards.title: NYSERDA Residential Energy Storage
cards.note: For new, permanent batteries of 25 kWh or less, installed by a participating contractor. NYSERDA says a project can generally get several thousand dollars.

cards.title: Higher rate for some homes
cards.note: NYSERDA pays more to income-eligible homeowners and homes in a Disadvantaged Community.

cards.title: NY-Sun solar (if you add panels)
cards.note: Solar is optional for the battery incentive here, but NY-Sun incentives and a 25% state tax credit help if you add it.

cards.title: Federal battery tax credit
cards.note: Does not apply to batteries placed in service after December 31, 2025.

after_cards:
Long Island is different

NYSERDA's program page says Long Island battery incentives go through PSEG Long Island and need solar. New York City homes are in the statewide program, which does not require solar. If a contractor tells you otherwise, ask them to show you the rule.
sections: Who in New York City can use this

Batteries go in houses more easily than apartments. The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts about 3.68 million homes in New York City. 9% are single detached houses and 21% are in buildings of 2 to 4 units. About 33% of households own their home. So the program fits a smaller group of New Yorkers: owners of detached, semi-detached, row and small multi-family houses.

If you rent, a battery is your landlord's decision. A portable power station you can carry is not part of this program, since NYSERDA requires a permanent, stationary system.
What a battery does for a city home

NYSERDA describes a home battery as a cabinet-sized unit in a garage, basement, on an outside wall or in the yard, depending on local permit rules. It charges from the grid or from solar. In an outage it keeps key things running, like lights, the fridge, and heating or cooling controls, for a set time. It may not power the whole house.

In New York City, 64% of homes heat with piped gas, per the same Census survey. A gas boiler or furnace still needs a little electricity to run. If outages are your worry, ask the installer to put the heating circuit on the backed-up panel.
Is it worth it without the federal credit?

Be clear-eyed. The federal 30% credit for batteries is gone for anything installed after 2025. The NYSERDA incentive is real, but it changes with each block of funding. For most families a battery is a comfort and resilience purchase, not a money maker. It pays best if you have someone at home who relies on medical equipment, if you work from home, or if your block loses power often.

If you want lower bills more than backup, solar or a heat pump will usually do more per dollar. Our New York City heat pump guide covers Con Edison's Clean Heat rebates, which are much larger.

Are you a NYSERDA participating storage contractor? What is the incentive per kWh today, and will it be locked when you apply? How many kWh is the battery, and which circuits does it back up? Who handles the city permits and the Con Edison interconnection? What does the warranty promise after ten years?
claim_heading: How to get the battery incentive in New York City
claim_steps: Find a participating contractor through NYSERDA's energy storage contractor list.
Get quotes for a battery of 25 kWh or less, with the NYSERDA incentive shown as its own line.
If your income may qualify, or you live in a Disadvantaged Community, ask about the higher rate.
The contractor applies to NYSERDA. The incentive lowers your price.
faq: Do I need solar panels to get a battery incentive in NYC?
No. NYSERDA's statewide Residential Energy Storage Program does not require solar. Only the Long Island program does.
25 kilowatt-hours or less, and it must be new, permanent and stationary, installed by a participating contractor.
How much is the NYSERDA battery incentive?
It is set per kWh, varies by region and changes over time. NYSERDA posts current rates on its residential incentive dashboard. Ask your contractor for today's rate in writing.
Is the federal battery tax credit still available?
No. The IRS says the Residential Clean Energy Credit does not apply to property placed in service after December 31, 2025.
Can a renter get a battery incentive?
Only the property owner can install a permanent battery. Talk to your landlord, since the system stays with the building.
